Refactor handoff validation

Source: vignettes/articles/contributor-tools-refactor-validation-readme.Rmd
contributor-tools-refactor-validation-readme.Rmd

Contributing · Object model · Discovery walkthrough · Object fields

Supporting record: claims apply to the revisions and environments named below; this page does not qualify a later candidate.

The refactor is prepared for maintainer review in PR #234. Start with the portable tour linked from the parent README, then use the lasting architecture guide to find the implementation files. Merge and release remain separate maintainer steps.

What was verified

Check Outcome
Fresh source build and R CMD check --no-manual Status OK, including examples and rebuilt vignettes
Permanent package tests 4,397 passing assertions; zero failures, warnings or skips on the recorded Mac run
Explicit original/current comparison 1,266 passing assertions in 31 blocks; backed coverage required; zero failures, errors, warnings or skips
Actual downstream R scripts All 30 original and candidate stages pass; ordered output payloads match exactly, with tolerance zero
Adversarial checks of permanent assertions Genuine outputs pass; all nine deliberately wrong outputs are rejected
Failed comparison reporting Unknown ref, old candidate and unqualified ondisc all exit nonzero and record failed, stage and error
Package contents Developer tooling absent; permanent tests and the older saved-object input retained
Test-input maintenance Four input-only recipes reproduce identical R objects; unused retired-sampler metadata removed from permanent inputs
Documentation generation Default roxygen generation completes without the former nested-tag/range warnings; generated help synchronized; Rcpp bindings unchanged
BiocCheck 0 errors, 1 warning, 5 notes under the recorded administrative flags; this is not submission approval

The package/test check uses source 47f76f63f4affa661b98a51d2916d218379acfc9. The old/new and actual-script runs use build 2f610015e26acf06d7179b099e96774b3d3f7a25. All 84 runtime-source and bundled-input files are byte-identical between those commits. Subsequent changes clean test metadata or add handoff documents; they do not change that implementation. source-files.json records the qualified package/test/CI file hashes, allowing later delivery-only commits to be checked without repeating numerical claims.

The manual total includes one explicit required-ondisc assertion; the earlier unflagged command reported 1,265. Coverage remains the separately recorded matched measurement, 70.65% to 84.16% of executable R lines. It is not a newly measured percentage for the final tests, and C++ line coverage has not been measured.

Completion audit dispositions

Finding Final disposition
Sampler tests checked repeatability more than probabilities Added individual/joint inclusion and successive-draw checks using independent Bernoulli and sampling-without-replacement formulas
Whole workflows could pass with invalid output Check meaningful rows, pair labels, independently calculated QC, toy effect direction and p-value bounds
Warning capture hid regressions Require no unexpected warnings in these supported workflow fixtures, including backed runs
Worker errors lost their cause Preserve cause and block number; distinguish failed/lost replies from successful empty results; test real child exit and empty internal CRT dispatch
Backed dependency requirement was buried Permanent installation guidance and companion matrix; manual preflight requires the guarded source when ondisc is present
Older saved-object compatibility lived only in temporary tools Permanent versioned input and current resumption test, without an old executable or old numerical-output snapshot
Permanent fixtures had no lasting maintenance path Input-only recipes and provenance; historical generation stays archived
Bug fixes lacked lasting release/help notes NEWS groups consequential behavior changes; import help explains duplicate-coordinate rejection
Readable architecture would retire with the tour Plain-language module map and cell-numbering example remain in the lasting guide
Status summaries and roadmap were stale Historical summaries archived unchanged; one current handoff index and updated roadmap
Evidence overwhelmed review Published full evidence tag; removed 787 historical files from the active tree, preserving Git history
Manual tool/report/reader delivery was incomplete Failed-status controls, guarded dependency preflight, immutable-source rendering and a portable two-page ZIP
Accepted debt lacked durable ownership Issues #235–#238 assigned to Eugene for resource, dependency, numerical and companion triage; maintainer review remains the next human step

Evidence and limits

receipt.json identifies measured source commits, flags, tarball hash and scope. The retained build/check/BiocCheck logs, manual per-contract CSV/log, negative controls and pipeline summary support the outcomes above. Absolute temporary paths in captured command records describe the actual runs; reproduce them using fresh paths and the commands in the parent README. Full historical raw evidence, specification and resource/Nextflow/book records remain at the published refactor-evidence-2026-10-16-e1f8109 tag.

The fresh consumer check executes actual pipeline R scripts, including standard and nuclear phases. It is distinct from the earlier complete Nextflow run, whose local matched arrival/seed scope and source pin remain recorded. Historical containers, arrays, hosted schedulers and whole-book rendering are not newly qualified. Selected book coverage remains 14/15 with the same inherited empty-barcode failure; issue #238 owns triage, without assuming its root cause.

The two separately accepted memory costs remain bounded and tracked in #235. The guarded ondisc release is tracked in #236. Inherited fully tied two-sided empirical tails can exceed one (#237); the refactor retains that formula and the new bound checks concern its nondegenerate toy workflows. These are explicit follow-ups, not hidden claims that all software defects have been eliminated.

One earlier package-check attempt failed because a proposed test bypassed the public zero-passing-QC guard and expected successful result assembly. The final test exercises supported empty internal dispatch instead; the public rejection rule is unchanged. Its source commit and disposition remain in receipt.json.

Consult the live PR checks for the final published head. Local checks do not assert that a future commit has passed CI, and no maintainer approval is implied.
